title: Client configuration guides
intro: Choose the client first, then check its input format. The GitHub and Cloudflare links in this project carry the same ordinary URI/Base64 node subscription for each language; they are not ready-made Clash/Mihomo YAML or native sing-box JSON profiles.
privacy: Keep private subscription URLs and credentials on your own device. Do not submit them to public conversion websites. If a different format is needed, obtain a compatible profile from your provider or prepare it locally using the target client's official configuration documentation.
limitations: Check the supported protocols and the installed core version; importing nodes does not guarantee that all rules, DNS settings or advanced fields will transfer.
uri: Add a supported node URL or ordinary URI/Base64 subscription in the client's subscription/profile area. Refresh the subscription and confirm that the expected nodes appear.
yaml: Obtain a complete Clash/Mihomo-compatible YAML profile. Import it as a local or remote profile, update it and select it. The ordinary subscription above is not a complete YAML profile.
singbox: Obtain a complete sing-box JSON profile matching the client's core version. Add it as a local or remote profile and update it. A list of node URLs or a Clash YAML file cannot be used as native sing-box JSON.
app: Obtain a complete profile in the format shown above. Import the local file or remote profile URL supported by this client, update it, and select that profile. Do not assume that ordinary node subscriptions or another app's configuration are interchangeable.
select: Where the profile offers a choice, select a node or proxy group, then enable the client’s documented proxy/VPN mode. Grant the operating-system VPN permission only to the official app you installed. Confirm actual access after connecting.
router: Before installation, check the firmware, CPU architecture, required packages and available memory. Back up the router configuration and keep a working management connection. Import only a supported subscription/profile, update it, choose the outbound node or group, and enable the plugin according to its official instructions.
troubleshoot: If updating fails, check the URL, network and HTTP error. If parsing fails, check the format and core version. If importing succeeds but connecting fails, refresh and try another supported node, then inspect the client's error log. A successful update or latency test does not guarantee availability or safety.
fallback: This concise guide covers the verified input format and basic workflow. The linked technical references are not a step-by-step user tutorial; interface labels can vary by version.
mixed: This client can read several formats, but use the ordinary URI/Base64 import route for this project's subscription. Native JSON and YAML profiles still have their own requirements.
nodeonly: Subscription import extracts supported nodes; do not assume that rules and other settings from the original profile are preserved.
homeproxy: HomeProxy manages nodes and subscriptions through its own interface. Check the formats supported by the installed version; using sing-box internally does not mean arbitrary full sing-box JSON profiles can be imported.
egern: Egern YAML is its own profile format, not Clash/Mihomo YAML.
quantum: Quantumult X uses its own configuration and remote server resources; a full configuration and a node resource are different inputs.
surge: Use a Surge configuration or managed configuration URL. Do not treat a general V2Ray subscription as a complete Surge configuration.
loon: Loon uses its own configuration and subscribed node formats. Verify each protocol and field rather than assuming full compatibility with Surge or Clash.
limited: Official user guidance is limited; use the concise setup steps and the verified official format reference below.
nodeapp: Prepare a node subscription or individual node configuration supported by this app. Add it using the app’s documented import method, update subscriptions where supported, and check that nodes appear. A node list and a complete routing profile are different inputs.
